context: Switch the three gates to the deployment-aware check, passing the deployment mode already resolved for the run where one is available and letting requires_cloud_storage_for_deployment() fall back to the platform-level answer when it is not (it already does this internally for platforms with no deployment_modes block). Keep requires_cloud_storage() itself unchanged — it has other callers, including benchbox/cli/cloud_storage.py::prompt_cloud_output_location, and narrowing it globally is a larger blast radius than this item wants. Add a registry-driven test that asserts the gate used by the run path agrees with requires_cloud_storage_for_deployment() for every registered platform's default deployment, so a future registry edit cannot silently reintroduce the divergence. Sequencing note: this item and the stage-classification item both edit benchbox/cli/orchestrator.py (this one at _apply_default_cloud_output_dir, that one at _resolve_custom_output_root and _resolve_construction_output_dir). The dependency is declared so the two are not worked in parallel.
description: Three call sites decide whether to pull a credential-stored default_output_location into the run: benchbox/cli/orchestrator.py::_apply_default_cloud_output_dir and two checks in benchbox/cli/commands/run.py::_interactive_cloud_setup_if_needed. All three gate on PlatformRegistry.requires_cloud_storage(), which is implemented as `metadata.get('category') == 'cloud'` — a coarse platform-level label. The registry already exposes the precise per-deployment answer via requires_cloud_storage_for_deployment(), and the two disagree. Verified on 2026-07-24 @ 14b0271c1 by enumerating the registry: of the 24 platforms whose category is 'cloud', three report requires_cloud_storage_for_deployment() == False for their DEFAULT deployment — firebolt (default deployment 'core', a free local Docker engine), motherduck (default 'managed') and starburst (default 'managed'). For those, a stored default_output_location is injected as the run's output root even though the selected deployment stages nothing remotely. That is the same failure shape that produced the in-repo '@~/benchbox' spill, just latent because no credentials are stored for those three today.

anti_patterns.instead: Ask the registry per run via requires_cloud_storage_for_deployment()
anti_patterns.why: The list is derived state that goes stale the moment a platform's deployment_modes block is edited

anti_patterns.dont: Redefine requires_cloud_storage() itself to consult deployment modes
anti_patterns.instead: Change only the three run-path gates to the deployment-aware call and pin the agreement with a test
anti_patterns.why: It has callers beyond the run path and a global narrowing changes prompting and validation behaviour well outside this defect

preserves.behavior: An explicit --output still short-circuits the whole gate before any credential lookup
Non-interactive runs still exit 1 when a cloud platform genuinely lacks credentials

Platforms whose default deployment genuinely stages remotely (snowflake, bigquery, databricks, redshift, athena, synapse, the Spark-on-cloud family) keep pulling their stored default_output_location exactly as today
requires_cloud_storage() keeps its current semantics for all other callers, including prompt_cloud_output_location

verifications.description: CLI orchestrator and run-command unit tests pass

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest -k 'cloud_storage_gate or requires_cloud_storage' -q

uv run -- python -c "from benchbox.core.platform_registry import PlatformRegistry as R; R._platform_metadata = R._platform_metadata or R._build_platform_metadata(); bad={n for n in R._platform_metadata if R.requires_cloud_storage(n) != R.requires_cloud_storage_for_deployment(n)}; assert bad=={'firebolt','motherduck','starburst'}, sorted(bad); print('confirmed', sorted(bad))"
verifications.description: Premise pin: the registry-level and deployment-level answers still diverge for exactly the three known platforms
verifications.expected: exit 0. This pins the registry premise and stays true after the fix - the registry is not changed, only the gate. The behavioural check is the parametrised gate test in verification 2.

work_units.evidence: Re-validated on develop @e51d0e34b (both batch deps merged): exactly {firebolt, motherduck, starburst} diverge between requires_cloud_storage() and requires_cloud_storage_for_deployment() across all 51 registered platforms -- no drift. Located the three run-path gates: orchestrator.py:380 (_apply_default_cloud_output_dir) and run.py:2204 + :2221 (both inside _interactive_cloud_setup_if_needed). Confirmed the run's deployment mode is carried in database_config.options['deployment_mode'] (registered per-platform via PlatformOptionSpec in cli/platform_defaults.py), so it can be threaded when present and left None to mean 'platform default deployment'.

work_units.evidence: Switched orchestrator._apply_default_cloud_output_dir to PlatformRegistry.requires_cloud_storage_for_deployment(type, deployment_mode). Added module-level _resolved_deployment_mode(database_config) that reads database_config.options['deployment_mode'] and returns None when unset, so the registry falls back to the platform's default_deployment. Docstring now states why the gate is deployment-scoped. requires_cloud_storage() itself is untouched.
work_units.summary: Switch benchbox/cli/orchestrator.py::_apply_default_cloud_output_dir to requires_cloud_storage_for_deployment(), threading the run's resolved deployment mode when available

work_units.evidence: Switched both requires_cloud_storage() checks in run.py::_interactive_cloud_setup_if_needed (:2211 early-return, :2228 credential lookup) to requires_cloud_storage_for_deployment(type, deployment_mode), early-return semantics identical. FOUND AND FIXED A REGRESSION the 3-gate scope would have shipped: with only those gates changed, an interactive firebolt/motherduck/starburst run skips cloud setup (s.output never set), is then NOT offered the local-output prompt at _interactive_prompt_output_and_format (gated on the category check), and finally hard-errors 'Cloud platform requires --output' in _interactive_preflight_and_execute -- a dead end with no way to satisfy it. Made those two remaining run-path gates deployment-aware too (same file, in only_modify). All 5 run-path gates now agree; requires_cloud_storage() itself is still untouched.
work_units.summary: Switch both requires_cloud_storage() checks in benchbox/cli/commands/run.py::_interactive_cloud_setup_if_needed to the deployment-aware call, keeping the early-return semantics identical

work_units.evidence: Added tests/unit/cli/test_cloud_storage_gate_deployment_aware.py (68 tests, all pass). Registry-driven and parametrised over all 51 platforms from PlatformRegistry._platform_metadata -- no hardcoded skip-list. Covers: gate answer == requires_cloud_storage_for_deployment() for every platform's default deployment; the divergence set is pinned to exactly {firebolt, motherduck, starburst} so a deployment_modes edit fails loudly; genuinely-remote platforms (snowflake/bigquery/databricks/redshift/athena/synapse) still gate True; deployment-mode threading incl. empty-string and None-config; and an AST guard asserting NO run-path gate in orchestrator.py or commands/run.py still calls the category-level requires_cloud_storage. Verified the AST guard is non-vacuous: it flags a category call and ignores the deployment call.
work_units.notes: Place it under tests/unit/cli/ alongside the gate it exercises, not tests/unit/core/. Use firebolt, motherduck and starburst as explicit negative cases so a registry edit that re-diverges them fails loudly instead of silently re-injecting an unused output root.
work_units.summary: Add a registry-driven parametrised test asserting the run-path gate matches requires_cloud_storage_for_deployment() for every platform's default deployment
